$comment: TransLink's GTFS feeds (packages/transit-core/DESIGN.md#source-data). Which routes are drawn: routes.json. Regions showing it: metro-vancouver.
name: TransLink

static.$comment: The undated zip is the latest feed and serves the same file as its dated History/ snapshot (fetched daily: not part of the Open API budget).

realtime.$comment: TransLink's GTFS-realtime (buses only: no SkyTrain, SeaBus or West Coast Express), polled by the server's leader only (apps/server/README.md#real-time-service). The key (TRANSLINK_API_KEY, in the environment or .secrets) never leaves the server.
realtime.$poll: TransLink's Open API terms allow an API key 'a maximum of 1,000 requests per day' (https://www.translink.ca/about-us/doing-business-with-translink/app-developer-resources/terms-of-use, checked 2026-09-29; unclear whether that covers GTFS-RT). Until TransLink says otherwise, the leader stays under dailyCap across all three feeds in any 24 hours (a ledger in var/rt-history/requests.json enforces it across restarts), polling most often at peak. Bands (local time) are guesses at when buses are busiest; at most ~970 in any 24 hours (~965 on a weekday, ~815 on a weekend day) (packages/transit-core/src/rt/budget.ts, test/rt-budget.test.ts). Holidays run the weekday schedule. SkyTrain alerts with a recognised operating change become draft disruptions (packages/transit-core/DESIGN.md#disruptions-and-alerts), so alertsS delays drafts by up to that long. OPEN-QUESTIONS #29.
realtime.$staleGraceS: Clients treat live data as unavailable (and fall back to schedule estimates) once it's this much older than the positions poll interval. Was 120 s at a fixed 20 s interval.
realtime.$coverageSlackS: Recorder coverage breaks when consecutive snapshots are further apart than the positions poll interval plus this. Was 75 s at a fixed 20 s interval.
realtime.$interpolateSlackS: Interpolate a vehicle between two observations only when they are at most the positions poll interval plus this apart. Was 180 s at a fixed 20 s interval.
realtime.$extrapolateSlackS: At the live edge, predict a vehicle forward along its route for at most the positions poll interval plus this (fixes are already ~20-60 s old when fetched). Was 90 s at a fixed 20 s interval.
realtime.$tripUpdatesMinCoverage: /healthz fails when fewer than this share of the vehicles in a positions poll (those on a trip) have a delay from TransLink's trip updates: the trip-updates feed is empty or no longer matches the positions. Measured 2026-10-01 to 10-11: 75-85 % in service hours, 36-60 % at night; 0 from 04:00 on 2026-10-12 while polls kept succeeding (apps/server/README.md#real-time-service). Guess at the threshold.
realtime.$tripUpdatesMinBuses: Coverage is judged only on positions polls with at least this many buses on a trip: with a handful, one bus is a large share. Guess.
realtime.$tripUpdatesLowForS: /healthz fails only once coverage has stayed below tripUpdatesMinCoverage (with enough buses) this long: the outage of 2026-10-12 lasted hours, while single polls can dip. Guess.

ais.$comment: Live vessel positions from aisstream.io (packages/transit-core/DESIGN.md#seabus-ais; key AISSTREAM_API_KEY in .secrets). The RT service's leader keeps one WebSocket open, records fixes to var/ais-history/translink/ and serves them by the day and in the live endpoint (<feed>/ais); the browser turns them into timetable anchors (packages/transit-core/src/ais/match.ts).
ais.$vessels: MMSIs from MarineTraffic / VesselFinder / MyShipTracking, cross-checked (2026-09-28). Burrard Beaver is the spare.
ais.$boundingBox: Burrard Inlet around the crossing and the layup berth, [[lat, lon], [lat, lon]] (aisstream order).
ais.$batchS: Fixes are recorded in batches this often (an empty batch while connected keeps recorder coverage going).
ais.$coverageGapS: AIS recorder coverage breaks when consecutive batches are further apart than this (was shared with the bus recorder before its polling slowed; config/regions/metro-vancouver/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md #29).
ais.$liveWindowS: The live endpoint carries the AIS batches of this long before the latest one. It must exceed the day file's edge-cache time (60 s, apps/server/src/rt/service.ts) plus the browser's longest poll interval (rt.json clientPollMaxS), so a browser that loaded the day file and then polls on schedule never misses a batch. Guess.
ais.$maxBackoffS: Reconnect backoff doubles from 5 s up to this.
ais.$match: Matching fixes to trips. 30-minute probe 2026-09-28 evening: per vessel in service, fixes a median ~60 s apart, gaps up to ~4 min; docked positions agree with the berth dock points to ~5 m. Guesses unless noted; config/regions/metro-vancouver/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md #27.

match.$maxOffsetM: Lanes are traced to ±30 m and vessels wander ~100 m around them (AIS tracks).
match.$minTurnaroundS: Timetabled layovers are 2–4 min; a late vessel catches up by shortening them to this.
match.$pairMinFixes: The day's berth pair is the one with at least this many docked fixes, more than at every other pair together; until then, defaultPair.

ais.$glide: When new fixes arrive, vessels glide to their corrected position instead of jumping (packages/transit-core/src/ais/glide.ts, like buses): drawn behind, they catch up at up to catchUpMps extra over minGlideS–maxGlideS; drawn ahead, they hold (≤ maxHoldS). Under minM nothing changes; over snapM they jump. Guesses: the SeaBus cruises at ~6 m/s (AIS: 11–12.7 kn), so +4 m/s is a visible but plausible hurry.
